findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:1142-1151 (Scenario: A reload after the replacement reads the page with no notice and claims no second replacement), with crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs:876 when_open and :1438 then_on_instance_page
findings.obligation: P2 and E6: a reload after the replacement reads the page with no notice and claims no second replacement; declared falsifier 'a notice carried in the address'
findings.observation: The scenario's When is the shipped step 'Priya opens the instance integrations page', which calls iis::when_open -> eip::when_open(world, who, INSTANCE_INTEGRATIONS): it requests the bare path, not the address Priya landed on. The landing assertion then_on_instance_page compares answer.path.split('?').next() == Some(INSTANCE_INTEGRATIONS), so it accepts a landing address carrying a query. An implementation that redirects to /admin/instance/integrations?replaced=2 and renders I-24 from the query therefore passes every scenario of this oracle, while the user's own reload - which re-requests the landed URL including its query - reads 'Replaced.' a second time and claims a second replacement. The acceptance record for the Confirming scenario states this gap and asserts 'only the reload case tells the two apart'; as written the reload case does not tell them apart, so the declared falsifier has no observation anywhere in the oracle.
findings.remediation: Reload the address Priya landed on, not the bare path: add a step (for example 'When Priya reloads the page she landed on') that re-GETs world.eip.when_answer's path with its query, and use it in this scenario. Optionally also assert that the landing address carries no notice in its query. One scenario and one support function; no other scenario changes.

findings.location: crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:1098-1112 (Scenario Outline: The replace page says how many saved credentials are sealed again, and reading it replaces nothing) and :1065-1077 (scenario 1)
findings.obligation: E3 / P1: opening the replace page, also more than once or as a prefetch, changes nothing the user can see - no new key, no re-sealing, no Activity line, AND no message on the integrations page afterwards
findings.observation: The oracle observes the first three clauses (then_nothing_replaced compares the stored key through the test seam and the whole Activity list). The fourth clause is unobserved: no scenario asserts that after only opening the replace page, the instance integrations page shows no 'Replaced.' notice. A GET that stores the one-shot I-24 notice in the session while writing nothing would pass this oracle, and Priya would then read 'Replaced.' on her next page view although no replacement happened. The reload scenario cannot catch it, because there the notice is expected to be consumed by a replacement that did happen.
findings.remediation: In the read-only outline (or scenario 1), after the Then that compares the stored key and the Activity, add an observation that the instance integrations page Priya reads next says nothing containing 'Replaced.' - the step 'nothing Priya reads there says "..."' already exists (feature_instance_integration_setup.rs:586) and is reachable for Priya after this commit.

findings.location: docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/acceptance.md ### S1, the P3 row: Disposition NotTested, owner 'DELIVER, the store write verification named by this slice's verification commands'
findings.obligation: P3 and E7: a failed re-seal changes nothing - the old key stays in effect, every credential still opens, the Activity records no replacement, AND the user sees no replaced message (the public oracle's expected observation: the refusal answers the confirm page again and no I-24 is read anywhere)
findings.observation: The NotTested disposition at the public port is justified and accepted: no listed public stimulus makes the re-seal closure refuse while the replace door is still offered (the state where the stored key cannot be opened withholds Replace entirely), and the compare-and-set losing half is constructed publicly by the simultaneous-replace scenario. The preservation map is incomplete on one half only: the named owner is the store write verification (scripts/test-in-lima.sh cargo test -p foundry-store --test iis_instance_store), which observes database state and cannot observe a response or the absence of the notice. The clauses 'the response is the confirm page again' and 'no I-24 is read anywhere' therefore have no named verification owner in any phase.
findings.remediation: Extend the P3 disposition's owner to name both halves: the store write verification for the unchanged state under an injected refusal, and the handler verification already in this slice's commands (scripts/test-in-lima.sh cargo test -p foundry-app --lib integrations::handlers, with a store double that refuses) for the answer - the confirm page again and no I-24 notice. Record it as a completion obligation of DELIVER; no new acceptance scenario is required.

diagnostic: Rejected on one concrete oracle defect; the rest of the S1 oracle is adequate and its RED is semantic. Adequacy of the criteria first: the selected contract preserves the agreed value (rotate the key she doubts with nobody reconnecting), the scope-out items are the human-authorized Deliverable A and Request 1-2 boundaries plus the storage/grace-window question DESIGN owns, and no promised outcome of US-IIS-07 AC 1 is narrowed away in S1 (AC 2-6, Start over and its I-26 gate, belong to the later slices and the feature file says so). The oracle drives the real public doors through the production router behind require_instance_admin, reads the stored key through the one declared test seam (so a page that merely prints I-24 cannot pass), asserts the Activity as a whole exhaustive list, and closes both directions of the obligation relation for E1, E2, E4, E5, E8, E9, E10's replaced line, E23 and E24. RED is measured and semantic, not infrastructure: 11 of 11 scenarios fail on the replace door answering 404 with 94 of 105 steps passing, every harness precondition green. P3's NotTested at the port is justified - no public stimulus makes the re-seal closure refuse while Replace is still offered. The blocker: the reload scenario, the only scenario whose purpose is to discriminate the one-shot session notice from a notice carried in the address, re-requests the bare /admin/instance/integrations instead of the address Priya landed on, and the landing assertion strips the query. An implementation that redirects to ...?replaced=2 passes the whole oracle while a real browser reload reads 'Replaced.' a second time, so P2's promised reload outcome has no falsifier - exactly what the acceptance record claims this scenario closes. Two further findings do not veto craft but stay open as completion obligations: E3's 'no message on the integrations page afterwards' is unobserved, and P3's NotTested owner names only the store write verification, which cannot observe the refusal's answer or the absent I-24. Fix the reload address, then re-review the corrected scenario and P2 only; every other judgment above is retained. typesafe: unavailable (exit 3, key absent) - all judgments local.
